# Compile an action video

Compile a promo video package — a short promo, a longer showreel and highlight clips — from captured gameplay, selecting exciting moments from recorded on-screen action-intensity peaks, guaranteeing weapons/pickups/enemies coverage, and compiling the cuts with ffmpeg at full game-native 960×540 resolution.

## Problem statement

Captured gameplay videos and per-run **on-screen action intensity** records (`.action.jsonl`) already exist, but no promo material has been assembled from them. The project needs a compelling promo video package that shows a wide range of gameplay features — weapons, pickups, enemies — at an attention-grabbing pace, produced reproducibly from the existing capture pipeline.

## Users

- **Primary — the maintainer / release owner.** Wants showcase material (promo, showreel, individual highlight clips) to demonstrate the game's variety and pace without manual screen recording or hand-editing.
- **Secondary — prospective players / viewers.** The audience of the promo: they should see dense, exciting action within seconds (hook) and a representative spread of gameplay features.

**User stories:**

- As the maintainer, I can run one command that compiles my captured footage into a short promo, a long showreel and highlight clips, so I can share the game attractively.
- As the maintainer, I can trust that the exciting moments are chosen from recorded action-intensity peaks, so the edits feature real on-screen action rather than idle segments.
- As the maintainer, I can see which features (weapons, pickups, enemies) each clip shows, so the promo covers the whole game.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Deliverables at full game-native resolution.** The work produces, written under the gitignored `capture-output/` tree: (a) a single compiled promo WebM of ~45–60 s, (b) a longer showreel WebM (>2 min), and (c) several short highlight clips — all WebM (VP9+Opus or VP8 fallback) at the game's **full native 960×540 resolution** (the game renders natively at 960×540: `src/core/constants.ts`), each carrying the game's own SFX audio track.
- **AC2 — Automated action-intensity peak selection.** The editing source pool and edit points are driven by the recorded per-run action-intensity series: peak windows (`burstiness ≥ 0.15` and/or `intensity ≥ 0.7`, merged within a 1.0 s gap, with lead/tail padding) as implemented by the existing pure helper (`src/scenes/core/actionIntensityHighlights.ts`) and the highlight recipe in `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.5. Each selected segment is verifiable: a selection manifest lists source WebM, `.action.jsonl`, mapped video timestamps, and the intensity values that motivated the pick.
- **AC3 — Feature coverage (editorial pass).** The compiled promo and showreel visibly demonstrate a **wide range of gameplay features — weapons, pickups, enemies** (a boss segment if footage is available). A **coverage manifest** accompanies the deliverables listing, per feature, which clip and timestamp ranges show it; all three feature categories are represented.
- **AC4 — Attention-grabbing pace.** The promo opens with action (no dead air in the first ~5 s) and cuts on peaks — verified by measured criteria: the promo's sampled non-black frame ratio stays high and its average recorded intensity is at or above the documented reference band, with the per-clip intensities printed in the manifest. Editing judgment (cut cadence, ordering) is specified in the compile script's editorial config so pace is intentional and reproducible, not accidental.
- **AC5 — Reproducible, committed compile pipeline.** A committed editor script (e.g. `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` + an `npm run compile:promo` script) drives the compilation **deterministically via ffmpeg** (installed on the host, per producer decision): trim, reorder, join and mux the source clips without hand-editing. The script (`--help`) documents inputs/outputs and prerequisites, fails with clear errors when ffmpeg or source footage is missing, and its pure parts (manifest/selection logic) are unit-tested hermetically.
- **AC6 — Testing/validation.** The pure selection/planning logic of the compile script has hermetic unit tests; the delivered video files are validated (decodable, non-trivial non-black pixels, audio track present, correct resolution) by a validation step in the pipeline.
- **AC7 — Documentation updated to reflect the changes**, including the compile pipeline, prerequisites (ffmpeg), command examples, manifest formats, and any relevant references in `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` / `docs/dev/action-intensity.md`.
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Game-native resolution only (960×540)** — no 1080p upscale; the game has no native 1080p detail (producer decision Q4=A).
- **ffmpeg as the joining tool** — a host-level dependency (not currently installed); the pipeline must document and detect it. No other new system dependencies (producer decision Q5=B).
- **`capture-output/` is gitignored** — deliverables themselves are never committed; only scripts, tests, docs and (small) manifests are committed.
- **Independent of multi-scene capture tooling** — do not block on *Scripted Gameplay Videos (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC)*; record it as related work only (producer decision Q3=A). Fade-transition re-filming is a possible future improvement, not a requirement here.
- **No manual screen recording / hand-editing** — everything flows from the existing capture pipeline outputs (`npm run capture`, `--all-scenarios`, demo runs) and recorded action-intensity series.
- Repo conventions apply: never edit `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/` or agent-infrastructure dirs; work item referenced in commits; UK English.

## Existing state

- `npm run capture` — headless-Playwright gameplay video capture: 960×540 WebM (VP9+Opus), 60 fps, with the game's own SFX (proven 2026-10-06). Flags: `--duration`, `--tail`, `--count`, `--all-scenarios`, `--scenario <name>`, `--list-scenarios`, `--scripted`, `--headed`, `--max-duration`.
- Action-intensity metric implemented and recorded per run as `<run-id>.action.jsonl` (per-tick `rawScore`/`intensity`/`smoothed`/`burstiness`) — *Implement on-screen action intensity metric (AH-0MUZMTTYH008KVS2)*, done.
- Time→video join helper (`capture_started` marker + `mapTimeToVideo`) and pure highlight window selection — `src/scenes/core/actionIntensityHighlights.ts` (+ tests), *Capture: video join + highlight selection (AH-0MUZQG13S006KL8K)*, done.
- Sample footage already in `capture-output/` (demo runs + `boss-four-hits` scenario clip).
- No ffmpeg on the host; no video-joining npm dependency.
- No promotion/compile tooling exists yet.

## Desired change

1. **Gather source footage** covering weapons, pickups and enemies at full native resolution (new `npm run capture -- --all-scenarios` and demo/full-run clips as needed).
2. **Automated highlight plan** — a script reads each source run's `.action.jsonl`, computes peak windows (reusing the documented highlight recipe), and produces an ordered edit plan (clip + in/out points) sized to the promo/showreel/clip target lengths.
3. **Editorial pass** — an editorial config guarantees feature variety (weapons, pickups, enemies each represented) and an attention-grabbing order: open on action, jump-cut across peaks, brief context shots where pacing benefits.
4. **Compile with ffmpeg** — a committed driver (`npm run compile:promo`) trims, orders, concats and muxes (audio preserved) into the three deliverables + manifests, validating outputs.
5. **Document & test** — docs for the pipeline and its prerequisites; hermetic unit tests for the pure plan/selection logic.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` (new) — ffmpeg-driven compile orchestrator: edit-plan generation, ffmpeg invocation, output validation
- `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts` (new) — hermetic tests for the pure edit-plan/selection logic (no ffmpeg, no browser)
- `scripts/compile-promo.d.mts` (new) — type declarations (repo convention for `.mjs` scripts)
- `package.json` — `compile:promo` script entry
- `src/scenes/core/actionIntensityHighlights.ts` — reference only: highlight thresholds/recipe to reuse (port the pure logic into the script where the TS helper is dev-gated/not importable from Node)
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` and/or `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` — § pipeline documentation, ffmpeg prerequisite, manifest formats
- `capture-output/` — deliverables + manifests (gitignored, never committed)

## Related work

- *Compile an action video (this item, AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX)* — top-level promo assembly.
- *Scripted Gameplay Videos (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC)* — related (not a blocker): future multi-scene capture with 0.25 s fades could replace cross-scene cuts; record as `related-to`.
- *Implement on-screen action intensity metric (AH-0MUZMTTYH008KVS2)* — done; provides the `.action.jsonl` series.
- *Capture: video join + highlight selection (AH-0MUZQG13S006KLK8)* — done; provides the highlight recipe and time mapping.
- *Spike: automated gameplay video capture (AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK)* — done; the capture pipeline producing source footage.
- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.5 — highlight recipe (peak thresholds, gap merge, lead/tail).
- *Screen action intensity tracking and analysis (AH-0MUZCSJXQ004TREN)* — done; research/decision behind the action-intensity metric (find-related).
- *SettingsScene: key-binding remapping + reset to defaults (AH-0MUA8BGE0006UAU4)* — completed, tangential (find-related).
- *Test matrix and shared fixtures for the collector-drone path (AH-0MVBMPYPB004RP0P)* — open, tangential (find-related).

## Risks & assumptions

- **ffmpeg availability (risk/mitigation):** host lacks ffmpeg; pipeline must detect its absence and fail with a clear installation message; document `apt`/`brew`/static-binary install in the docs. CI/other hosts need the same prerequisite — noted as an assumption that the operator's build hosts can install it, else this becomes a blocker to raise.
- **Native resolution ceiling (assumption):** "full resolution" = game-native 960×540; any 1080p/social-platform requirements are out of scope (follow-up item if ever needed).
- **Highlight pool quality (risk):** automated peaks may pick repetitive or visually similar moments; the editorial config + coverage manifest are the mitigation (variety, dedupe by feature, manual overrides allowed in the edit plan).
- **Scope creep (risk):** multi-scene fades (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC), 1080p output, audio editing, or a social-platform pipeline are explicitly **out of scope**; if discovered during implementation, record as new linked work items (`discovered-from:AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX`) rather than expanding this item.
- **Existing capture format assumption:** source footage is WebM (VP9+Opus) 960×540 as produced by `npm run capture`; ffmpeg trims/concat/muxes against that container (Opus audio preserved).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (Map, to producer): "Deliverable shape — (A) one compiled ~45–60 s WebM at 960×540 like existing captures / (B) longer showreel >2 min / (C) several short highlight clips?" — **ANSWERED: "All of the above but at full resolution."** Interpretation: produce all three deliverables (promo, showreel, highlight clips) at full game-native resolution — resolution clarified in Q4. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2 (Map, to producer): "How should exciting segments be chosen and ordered? (A) fully automatic peaks / (B) automated peaks + editorial pass for variety and pace / (C) fully manual." — **ANSWERED: B** — automated peak selection as source pool plus an editorial pass guaranteeing weapons/pickups/enemies coverage and attention-grabbing pacing. Source: interactive reply.
- Q3 (Map, to producer): "Relationship to multi-scene capture tooling (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC)? (A) independent / (B) dependent, wait for fades / (C) defer until tooling lands." — **ANSWERED: A** — independent; compile from existing single-scene captures; multi-scene tooling recorded as related work only. Source: interactive reply.
- Q4 (Map, to producer, round 2): "The game renders natively at 960×540 — what does 'full resolution' mean? (A) game-native 960×540 / (B) 1080p upscale (needs ffmpeg or a game-resolution change)." — **ANSWERED: A** — game-native full resolution (960×540); no 1080p upscale. Source: interactive reply.
- Q5 (Map, to producer, round 2): "No ffmpeg on the host; how should clips be joined? (A) browser-based edit console re-recording via captureStream / (B) install ffmpeg, drive from a Node script / (C) defer to multi-scene tooling." — **ANSWERED: B** — install ffmpeg on the host and drive it from a committed Node script. Source: interactive reply.

Research summary: the capture pipeline (`npm run capture`) and the action-intensity series (`.action.jsonl`) are complete and sample footage already exists in `capture-output/`; the pure highlight recipe lives in `src/scenes/core/actionIntensityHighlights.ts` and `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.5. The game's native resolution is fixed at 960×540 (`src/core/constants.ts`), and ffmpeg is not installed on the host (`which ffmpeg` — none), which the operator resolved by choosing to install it.

## Plan: decomposition

Decomposed into 9 child work items covering all 8 acceptance criteria (100 % AC
coverage verified by the `tree_coverage` review). Test-first ordering: the
hermetic test suite (AH-0MVDV47VO0081VUK) is created before the pure
implementation (AH-0MVDV4OKN001OT18), and the full-suite verification
(AH-0MVDV560Z002PSLT) depends on every implementation/doc child.

| # | Child | ACs covered | Depends on |
|---|-------|-------------|-----------|
| 1 | Capture: export action-intensity series + join anchor (AH-0MVDV4DMY001Z7CU) | prerequisite for AC2 | — |
| 2 | Tests: pure compile-promo edit-plan and selection (AH-0MVDV47VO0081VUK) | AC6 (test-first) | — |
| 3 | Implement: pure edit-plan and selection logic (AH-0MVDV4OKN001OT18) | AC2 | 1, 2 |
| 4 | Editorial config and feature-coverage manifest (AH-0MVDV4RJ300459ZF) | AC3, AC4 | 3 |
| 5 | ffmpeg compile driver and output validation (AH-0MVDV4PNZ004ZWOZ) | AC5, AC6 | 1, 3, 4 |
| 6 | Gather source footage covering weapons/pickups/enemies (AH-0MVDV4SYG008X8TY) | AC3 (source pool) | 1 |
| 7 | Produce and validate promo/showreel/highlight clips (AH-0MVDV50Z20071RF4) | AC1 | 5, 6 |
| 8 | Documentation for the promo compile pipeline (AH-0MVDV53RA0079F8N) | AC7 | 5, 7 |
| 9 | Full project test suite passes (AH-0MVDV560Z002PSLT) | AC8 | 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 |

Vertical-slice note: child 1 is a capture→disk slice (series + anchor);
children 2–4 are a pure logic slice (tests → selection → editorial);
child 5 is the ffmpeg slice; child 7 is the end-to-end runtime slice
(pool → deliverable + manifests + measured pace); child 8 is the docs slice.

### Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-18** — Initial decomposition by the `plan` skill:
  - Created 9 children (see table) and wired 16 dependency edges.
  - Ran the six automated review stages and the AC-coverage review
    (100 %, `proceed`).
  - Recorded the discovered capture-side series/anchor export gap (see
    Appendix P1) and created child 1 to close it.
  - Effort/risk re-estimated by the `effort_and_risk` skill.

## Appendix: planning questions & answers

The five producer decisions Q1–Q5 recorded in the intake Appendix above remain
the authoritative answers; they were re-read (not re-asked) during planning.

- **P1 — DISCOVERY, 2026-10-18 (Map, planning session).** Repository
  investigation found that the parent's "Existing state" claim that
  per-run `<run-id>.action.jsonl` records already exist is **not yet true**:
  no `.action.jsonl` files exist in `capture-output/`, and the pure serialiser
  `src/scenes/core/actionIntensitySerialiser.ts` has **no production caller**
  (only its unit test). `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` writes only the WebM;
  telemetry (with `state.actionIntensity`) is held in the page's JSONL sink
  (`localStorage` key `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl`). The §7.5 join inputs
  (`capture_started` epoch ms from `buildCaptureStartedMarker`, and the
  telemetry run-header `startedAt`) are produced in memory but not persisted
  next to the WebM.
  - **Resolution (assumption, documented for review):** close the gap by
    wiring `npm run capture` to persist `capture-output/<run-id>.action.jsonl`
    plus a join-anchor sidecar, reusing the **already-documented** §7.3 format
    and the existing pure serialiser — child *Capture: export
    action-intensity series + join anchor (AH-0MVDV4DMY001Z7CU)*. This is the
    minimal path mandated by AC2 (which requires a `.action.jsonl` per run)

    (none), `git log -S serialiseActionIntensitySeries` (serialiser commit
    only), `grep -rn serialiseActionIntensitySeries src/ scripts/` (no
    production caller).
  - **OPEN QUESTION (to producer, non-blocking):** if you would prefer the
    compiler to instead derive the series from a `npm run record`
    telemetry dump (rather than having `npm run capture` write it), say so and
    child 1 will be re-scoped. Recommendation: keep the capture-side export
    (it matches docs §7.3 and keeps WebM + series co-located).
- **P2 — ASSUMPTION (Map, planning session).** The parent AC4 "documented
  reference band" for average recorded intensity is **not yet documented**
  anywhere in `docs/dev/`. Planned resolution: child 7 documents the band
  (with its calibration basis) and child 8 records it in the docs; the band is
  derived from the captured peak windows rather than fixed a priori.
  - **OPEN QUESTION (to producer, non-blocking):** do you want a specific
    minimum mean-intensity threshold (e.g. ≥ 0.4) written into the docs, or is

    Recommendation: calibration-derived band, documented with the measured

# Enemies should be aware of the wrap around

## Problem statement

Enemies are currently "wrap-blind": aimed shots always fire a straight line at
the player's raw position (never crossing a screen edge), and enemy movement is
bounded or clamped to the arena, so no enemy ever flies over a screen edge the
way the player ship, asteroids, bullets and the raider patrol already do. The
playfield seam is therefore one-directional — only the player's shots and the
player can cross it — letting the player camp the edges with impunity. Enemy
behaviour should be wrap-aware by default — firing across the seam to reach the
player and flying over the edges — controlled by a per-enemy parameter so a
small set of classic arcade archetypes (Space Invaders march, Centipede) keeps
its bounded, wall-respecting behaviour.

## Users

- **Players** — enemy shots can now arrive from anywhere, including from
  "off-screen" across the seam, so camping a screen edge is no longer a safe
  position. Most enemies occupy the whole wrap-around world rather than a
  bounded box, while the classic set pieces (Space Invaders, Centipede) stay
  recognisible.
- **AI agents / human developers** — one unambiguous data-driven per-archetype
  parameter (`wrapAware`, default `true`) that the game and every gym read
  through the same shared seams, so game↔gym parity is preserved by
  construction and tuning an archetype is a one-field change.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want enemies to fire at me across the screen edge, so that
  hiding against an edge is no longer a guaranteed safe position and shots can
  arrive from the seam exactly like my own wrapped bullets.
- As a **player**, I want most enemies to fly over a screen edge and reappear on
  the opposite side, so the whole wrapped playfield — not a bounded box — is
  part of the arena.
- As a **player**, I want the Space Invaders block and the Centipede to keep
  their classic behaviour (reversing at the walls / weaving within the arena),
  so those recognisable set pieces remain intact.
- As a **developer**, I want a single data-driven `wrapAware` parameter per
  archetype (default: aware) that behaves identically in the game and every
  gym, so enabling or disabling seam-awareness is a one-field change with no
  divergent copies.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Parameter** — Each enemy archetype carries a data-driven boolean
   `wrapAware` (or equivalently named) parameter, defaulting to `true`, wired
   through the existing `EnemyConfig` pipeline so it is visible and editable in
   the enemy editor panel. The `march` (Space Invaders) and `centipede` seed
   configs set it to `false`.
2. **Seam-aware aimed fire** — Aimed shots (Scout, march and the raider's
   aimed fire — every archetype routed through the aimed-shot method) fire
   along the shortest wrapped path to the player: when the direct line is
   longer than the wrap-around route, the shot leaves one edge and arrives from
   the opposite edge (enemy bullets already wrap; AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0). An
   enemy with `wrapAware: false` keeps the current direct aim.
3. **Wrap-aware movement** — Wrap-aware enemy motion (dive, chase, orbit,
   drift, roam, hold-and-move, etc.) that would carry the enemy off-screen
   wraps to the opposite edge (matching the player/asteroid four-edge wrap
   model) instead of being clamped. Non-aware archetypes (`march`,
   `centipede`) are unchanged: march reverses and drops at the arena edge;
   centipede weaves within bounds.
4. **Gym ↔ game parity** — The behaviour is implemented once in the shared
   core (`src/scenes/core/`) and exercised by the affected gym scene(s) and
   `PlayScene` in the same change, so the repo-wide duplicate-body / parity
   guards stay green.
5. **Testing, validation & docs** — Unit tests cover: seam-aware aim angle for
   wrap-aware enemies vs. direct aim for non-aware enemies; position wrapping
   on crossing each edge for wrap-aware motion; config default / CSV wiring
   including the `march` / `centipede` exclusions. The affected documentation
   (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` and any config-format docs) is
   updated to reflect the change. The full project test suite passes with the
   new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not change the bullet wrap model itself — enemy bullets already wrap and
  expire by lifetime (AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0); this item changes launch direction
  and enemy movement only.
- Exclusions are an explicit seed-config list: only `march` and `centipede`
  default to non-aware. During planning, any other archetype whose classic
  design requires wall interaction belongs in the exclusion list, recorded as a
  code comment and a documented divergence per the gym↔game parity convention
  (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).
- Implement through the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`), never a divergent
  copy, so the game and every gym run the same code.
- Out of scope: boss behaviours, player ship, minerals, drops, and the bullet
  wrap model itself.
- Written in UK English per repo convention.

## Existing state

- Enemy aimed fire: `Scout.tryFireAimedBullet` computes
  `heading = atan2(target.y - y, target.x - x)` on **raw** positions with no
  seam consideration — the same aimed-shot method is reused for march and
  raider via `ENEMY_FIRE_METHODS` (`src/entities/enemyFire.ts`).
- Enemy bullets: wrap all four screen edges and expire by lifetime
  (AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0; shared bullet path in `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`).
- Enemy movement: bounded. Ghost/Grunt clamp to `GAME_WIDTH`/`GAME_HEIGHT`;
  march reverses and drops at arena bounds (`src/scenes/core/marchFormation.ts`:
  `computeMarchBounds` / `advanceMarch`); centipede weaves within bounds;
  formation drift pushes rightward.
- Wrap model to match: player ship and `Asteroid.updatePosition` four-edge
  wrap; `Raider` patrol already wraps; `LaneTraffic` wraps horizontally.
- Enemies are data-driven: `EnemyConfig` (`src/core/configTypes.ts`) + seed
  defaults (`src/core/configDefaults.ts`) + CSV (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`)
  + enemy editor panel + gym editor.

## Desired change

1. Add the boolean parameter to `EnemyConfig` (`wrapAware`), seed default
   `true`; set `march` and `centipede` to `false`.
2. Seam-aware aim: for wrap-aware entities, compute the player delta along the
   shortest wrapped path before `atan2` in the shared aimed-fire seam; used by
   Scout / march / raider aimed fire (and any other archetype sharing the
   aimed-shot method).
3. Shared post-motion edge wrap: in the shared scene entity loop (game +
   gyms), wrap each wrap-aware enemy's position when it crosses an edge; gate
   on the flag so non-aware archetypes are untouched.
4. Verify per-archetype that nothing breaks (divers mid-dive, chasers,
   orbiters, swarm, formation drift) and adjust tests.
5. Update key docs (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`; config-format
   docs if they enumerate fields).

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — add `wrapAware?: boolean` to `EnemyConfig`.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — seed defaults: `true` for most archetypes;
  `false` for `march` and `centipede`.
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — new `wrapAware` column entries (if the CSV
  persists the field).
- `src/entities/enemyFire.ts` + aimed-fire call sites (`Scout.tryFireAimedBullet`,
  march, `Raider`) — seam-aware aim.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — expose the flag and any shared seam support.
- `src/scenes/core/` — shared post-motion wrap (CombatCoreScene / CombatScene
  shared entity loop, alongside the `enemyTargeting.ts` seams).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` + affected gym scenes
  (`GymFodderEnemies`, `GymCentipede`, …) — parity exercises.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — document the parameter and the
  exclusions.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: gameplay feel** — seam-aware aimed fire lets shots come from
  unexpected directions; mitigated by limiting the change to aimed shots
  (radial/spread remain direction-symmetric) and excluding the classic
  archetypes.
- **Risk: wrap × state-machine interaction** — a post-motion wrap applied to
  every wrap-aware archetype could interact with steering that seeks the player
  or with dive/common state machines near the seam (oscillation). Mitigation:
  per-archetype verification during planning and dedicated unit tests at the
  seam.
- **Risk: formation-drift scope** — drift formations that push off-screen wrap
  at the entity level; formation *bases* and shaping logic stay as-is.
- **Scope-creep guard** — seam-aware spread/radial patterns (Q2 option b) are
  out of scope; if wanted later they are tracked as a new work item, not added
  here. Any extra archetype exclusion discovered during planning becomes a new
  work item or is documented as a divergence, not silent scope growth.
- **Assumption: config plumbing** — the parameter lives in `EnemyConfig`
  (CSV-backed, editor-editable), consistent with the established data-driven
  enemy tooling; default `true` for all archetypes except the explicit
  exclusions.

## Related work

- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** — "Bullets should have a distance and should wrap
  around the screen" (completed). Bullets already wrap; this item builds
  directly on that model for launch direction.
- **AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW** — "Enemies should emerge from the wormhole" (open).
  Touches the same shared enemy spawn/motion seams; potential overlap to watch
  during planning.
- **AH-0MU4KQ6NT006MP52** — "Extract common enemy base class for regular
  enemies" (completed). `BaseEnemy` hosts the shared config/seam support.
- **AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN** — "Enemy Design tooling" (completed). The
  data-driven `EnemyConfig` pipeline this parameter extends.
- **AH-0MTAN4X5D009D7U6** — "Write ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md
  best-practice guide" (completed). The doc updated by AC 5.
- **AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1** — gym↔game parity convention (referenced in
  `AGENTS.md`), enforced by `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Movement scope: which enemies should actually 'fly over the edge'? (a)
  All wrap-aware archetypes — shared post-motion wrap in scene loops;
  march/centipede excluded. (b) Firing only. (c) A curated subset."
  — Answer (Map): "(a)". Source: interactive reply, intake round 1.
- Q2: "Firing scope: which fire patterns become seam-aware? (a) Aimed shots
  only. (b) All patterns."
  — Answer (Map): "(a)". Source: interactive reply, intake round 1.

# Balance the levels of all enemy sounds

> **Headline:** Enemy SFX levels are wildly inconsistent (measured ~7.9× peak and ~9.3× RMS spread across the 26 enemy cue assets, with one near-clipping outlier), and their pitched content is not anchored to the battle-scenes' musical scale. This item rebalances every enemy cue onto category-relative amplitude tiers and snaps all pitched oscillator automation to A natural minor, using the ToneForge `tf analyze` tooling to measure and verify.

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** bug

## Problem statement

Some enemy SFX are significantly louder than others, which distorts the mix and makes enemy actions inconsistent to read by ear. Measured over the 26 committed enemy cue assets in `public/audio/sfx/`: peak amplitudes span **0.059 → 0.465 (~7.9×)** and RMS spans **0.014 → 0.128 (~9.3×)**; the Scout fire shot (`weapon-laser-zap.1.wav`, RMS 0.298, peak 0.977, near-clipping) is roughly 4× louder than every other enemy cue even after the existing 0.5× runtime scale. In addition, enemy cue pitches are arbitrary frequencies rather than notes of the battle-scenes' musical scale, so the SFX do not sit in the tonal world of the game.

## Users

- **Players** — need consistent, legible audio feedback: enemy fire, advance warnings, spawns and destruction booms should read at coherent relative loudness, with no cue jumping out of the mix or hurting the ears.
- **Producer / audio direction (Ross)** — needs enemy SFX to sit in the *selected battle-scenes scale* (provisionally **A natural minor**), uniform within tier, so the palette matches the game's musical identity.
- **Developers** — need measurable invariants (amplitude tiers + scale conformance) encoded in a guard test so the balance cannot silently regress on later recipe edits.

User stories:

- As a player, I want no enemy sound to blast louder than the rest, so I can track threats by ear without volume jumps.
- As a producer, I want every enemy cue's pitched content to land on a note of the battle-scenes scale, so the SFX feel part of the game's musical world.
- As a developer, I want the amplitude/scale invariants enforced by an automated check, so future recipe changes that break the balance fail the build.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Analysis report committed:** `tf analyze` is run over every committed enemy cue asset; a deterministic, documented report (peak, RMS, crest factor, spectral centroid, duration per cue; pre-change spread of ~7.9× peak / ~9.3× RMS called out) is committed (predicted `docs/AUDIO_ENEMY_BALANCE.md`), including the post-change values.
- [ ] **AC2 — Category-relative amplitude tiers:** every enemy cue asset sits within **±1.5 dB** of its documented category RMS target — Ambience `dive-loop` ≤ 0.02; Subtle one-shots (spawn, advance, light fires, dive-start, bullet-destruction) target 0.055; Heavy one-shots (destructions, tank-fire, boss-fire/hit/phase-cue/spawn, boss-phase-transition) target 0.090 — with every peak ≤ **0.50**, no clipping, and multi-seed variant ranges (enemy-destruction, diver-destruction) internally consistent (< 0.5 dB across variants).
- [ ] **AC3 — Scale conformance (A natural minor):** every pitched-oscillator automation point (start / end / waypoints) in every enemy recipe snaps to the nearest **A natural minor** note (`A B C D E F G`, equal temperament, A4 = 440 Hz). Filtered-noise-only cues are documented as unpitched / conformant-by-nature. The multi-seed pitch-jitter ranges are re-derived as **scale-degree variants** (each seed starts on a different A-minor note and descends to an A-minor note), preserving per-kill variation without off-scale pitches.
- [ ] **AC4 — Scout fire resolved:** the scout fire shot (`playScoutFireSound`, currently the near-clipping existing-recipe asset `weapon-laser-zap.1.wav`) is brought into a target tier — recommended via a new in-repo baked recipe `aihell-scout-fire` preserving the "high square laser sweep" character — and the existing `TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE` (0.5×) runtime behaviour is unchanged (its tests still pass).
- [ ] **AC5 — Validation, docs, full suite:** a guard test asserts AC2 + AC3 over every enemy entry in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` (via the audio build/verify path, e.g. extended `build-audio` verification) and passes with the new assets (`npm run build-audio:verify`); all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (recipe amplitude tiers + scale table in `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`, README/guide references, code comments); the full project test suite and `npm run build` (including the audio render + checksum update) pass.

## Constraints

- **Never edit the `../ToneForge` sibling checkout** (repo rule, `audio/toneforge/README.md`). Any fix to the shared existing-recipe Scout fire asset must be a game-side in-repo recipe, not a ToneForge edit.
- **Deterministic pipeline:** recipes stay seed-reserved and data-only; `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` must be regenerated; reproducibility (render twice → byte-identical) must hold; `npm run build-audio:render` is the render path.
- **Runtime behaviour unchanged except through assets:** the audio pipeline (baked WAV via Phaser, master SFX gain, beat-accent scheduling, `TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE` 0.5, burn-time scale constants) is not rearchitected; balance changes are baked into recipes/assets (plus at most a cue-routing change for Scout fire).
- **Scale is provisional:** A natural minor is the agreed default for this item (operator-confirmed), pending the Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W); any reconciliation if that chapter documents a different battle scale is a small separate follow-up, not scope here.
- Game ↔ gyms parity: no gameplay behaviour changes are involved; any `effects.ts` touch must keep the shared path identical everywhere.
- UK English; Markdown; all project rules apply (tests via the test skill, commit hygiene, work-item association).

## Existing state

- The enemy cue set (26 assets) and their `tf analyze` metrics: spawn (enemy-spawn 0.068 RMS), destruction (enemy 0.098, diver 0.085, boss 0.128), advance (tank 0.091, scout/phaser 0.056), fire (tank 0.121, boss 0.104, diver 0.044, phaser 0.036, swarm-burst 0.038, scout = `weapon-laser-zap` 0.298/0.977 peak), dive (dive-start 0.069, dive-loop 0.014), boss (spawn 0.073, hit 0.095, phase-cue 0.098, phase-transition 0.069), bullet-destruction 0.067.
- All pitched automation values are currently arbitrary frequencies (e.g. enemy-spawn 220→880 Hz already in A minor; tank-fire 90→28 Hz, phaser-advance 660→880 Hz are off-scale).
- The `weapon-laser-zap.1.wav` Scout fire asset nearly clips (peak 0.977) and is the single worst offender.
- Music/scale terminology is not yet in the GDD (only "out of MVP scope" §7.3); the GDD Audio Design Chapter work item exists but is unimplemented.

## Desired change

- Analyse every enemy cue with `tf analyze` and commit the report.
- Edit the enemy recipes: retune per-node gain to the tier targets (verify with `tf analyze` on the rendered WAVs) and snap every pitched automation point to the nearest A natural minor note; convert jitter ranges to scale-degree variants; add a balanced in-repo `aihell-scout-fire` recipe and re-point `playScoutFireSound` at it.
- Re-render via `npm run build-audio:render` (updates WAVs + checksums), run the guard test and full suite, and update the docs.

**Key Files:**
- `audio/toneforge/recipes/*.yaml` — enemy recipes: gain-tier tuning + scale-note automation points (25 recipes; multi-seed variants enemy-destruction, diver-destruction, boss-phase-cue); new `aihell-scout-fire.yaml`
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` — add `aihell-scout-fire` cue entry (and retire/swap `weapon-laser-zap` for `playScoutFireSound`) if AC4 option chosen
- `public/audio/sfx/` and `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` — re-rendered enemy assets + digests
- `docs/AUDIO_ENEMY_BALANCE.md` (new) — `tf analyze` report, amplitude tier table, A-minor scale table, variant mappings
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — amplitude tier + scale-conformance columns for enemy cues
- `src/audio/effects.ts` (+ `src/audio/effects.test.ts`) — scout-fire asset routing change only
- guard test (new or extended, e.g. `scripts/build-audio.test.ts` / `src/audio/enemyBalance.test.ts`) — asserts AC2 + AC3 from `manifest.json` against committed WAVs
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 note that enemy cues are pitched to A natural minor (small)

## Related work

- **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — open; will document "Recommended Scales & Modes" — source of the future battle-scale reconciliation.
- **Switch game audio from procedural Web Audio to ToneForge (AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J)** — parent epic; this item is post-migration SFX palette work.
- **Reduce the volume of shots for Tank and Scout (AH-0MV74ROYR009X8U3)** — completed; established `TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE` 0.5 precedent for enemy-fire loudness.
- **Deterministic WAV build pipeline (AH-0MUTYV8FU007X7JD)** — completed; the render/verify/checksum machinery this item re-runs and extends.
- **Cue-to-recipe mapping and unused-cue audit (AH-0MUTYV7SQ005HURT)** — completed; authoritative cue catalogue updated here.
- **Update audio documentation (AH-0MUTYV9QV0000HDT)** — completed; documented the asset pipeline the docs updates touch.
- **Automate the balance-tuning loop (AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715)** — in progress; gameplay tuning CLI, distinct scope (note as potential future home for the audio guard).
- **Improve thruster audio (AH-0MV01G4NL009JK92)** — completed; established the ≤ 0.2 player-cue ceiling the enemy tiers sit alongside.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Provisional scale (assumption):** A natural minor is the agreed default; if the Audio Design Chapter later specifies a different battle scale, the A-minor conformance needs re-snapping (small follow-up, tracked on AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W). Documented in the brief and the recipe catalogues.
- **Scout fire character drift (medium):** replacing `weapon-laser-zap` with an in-repo recipe preserves the "high square laser sweep" intent rather than the exact bytes; audition to confirm, and document intent in the recipe.
- **Jitter → scale-degree variants (medium):** the pitch-variation distribution changes from free ±15 % to discrete scale degrees; verify by audition that repeated kills still feel varied (three A-minor anchor notes per range keep variety).
- **Build cost (low-medium):** re-rendering the full enemy set takes minutes (`npm run build` already ~5 min, cf. AH-0MV87694J009Z34V); the auto-mode fingerprint forces the needed re-render once; verify path (`build-audio:verify`) is fast.
- **Scope creep:** player / weapon / power-up / victory/defeat cues have their own documented volume ceilings and are intentionally out of scope; any imbalance found in them later becomes a separate linked item.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What is 'the selected scale' for the battle scenes?" — Answer (operator): "(b) Default to A natural minor (Aeolian)". Source: interactive reply, 2nd round after repo search found no documented scale (GDD §7.3 still says music out of MVP scope; Audio Design Chapter AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W unimplemented). Prior answer attempt: none accepted — first round answered "check GDD/audio design doc; ask again if absent"; repo check confirmed absent, Q1 re-asked and answered (b). Adopted as the conformance scale (AC3).
- Q2: "Amplitude balancing policy ('reasonable spread')?" — Answer (operator): "(b) Category-relative targets". Source: interactive reply. Adopted as AC2 (three tiers + ambience, ±1.5 dB window).
- Q3: "What counts as 'falling on a scale note' for frequency conformance?" — Answer (operator): "(a) Snap every pitched-oscillator automation point; noise-only cues conformant-by-nature". Source: interactive reply. Adopted as AC3.
- Issue-type decision: set to **bug** (corrects incorrect/inconsistent audio output); operator offered no objection when informed.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUBYSNGU0051XVO** – Pop SFX: playPowerUpCollectPopSound() with unit test (completed)
- **AH-0MUDY2ID7006VY3A** – Dedicated player-destruction SFX (completed)
- **AH-0MTGS9DZ6001IFJR** – Update GDD audio design section and code comments (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: amplitude, balance, enemy, ensure, fall, frequency, levels, note, others, scale, scenes, selected, sfx, should, sounds, spread, they, tooling, using
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: amplitude, balance, enemy, fall, frequency, levels, note, scale, scenes, selected, sfx, should, sounds, spread, tooling, using
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: balance, enemy, fall, levels, note, scale, scenes, selected, sfx, should, sounds, spread, tooling, using


## Post-audit fix: Phaser fire-sequence loudness (2026-10-19)

**Audit rejection (2026-10-18, producer):** "The Phaser is still way too loud."

**Diagnosis:** The Phaser was the only enemy fire sequence still played at **full runtime volume**. Tank and Scout run their advance+fire pairs through `TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE` (0.5×, AH-0MV74ROYR009X8U3), so their advance cues play at an effective RMS of ~0.028, while `playPhaserAdvanceCue()` (0.6 s rising sine, baked RMS 0.0564) and `playPhaserFireSound()` (0.1 s triangle, baked RMS 0.0550) played unscaled — the sustained Phaser tell therefore read ~6 dB louder than every other advance cue. The baked assets already sat inside the AC2 Subtle tier, so the numeric guard was green while the audible mix was not.

**Fix chosen (runtime trim, mirroring the established precedent):** add `PHASER_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE = 0.5` in `src/audio/effects.ts` and apply it to both `playPhaserAdvanceCue()` and `playPhaserFireSound()`. The baked assets, recipes and `checksums.json` are unchanged, so the AC2 amplitude-tier guard and the AC3 scale guard remain green; the trim sets the effective playback level to ~0.028 RMS for both cues, level with the Tank/Scout advance cues. This is a balance change expressed through the same named-constant mechanism the game already uses (`TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE`, `HOLD_FULL_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE`, `THRUSTER_HUM_SIDE_VOLUME_SCALE`) rather than a pipeline change; it is the minimal, tunable, testable fix. The no-gap advance→fire scheduling and `PHASER_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION` are unchanged.

**Constraint note:** the parent constraint prefers balance changes to be baked into assets. A runtime trim was chosen here because the baked Phaser assets are already correctly tiered (and the guard pins them); the audible problem is the missing playback trim relative to the Tank/Scout precedent. This is documented as a small, deliberate deviation, recorded in `docs/AUDIO_ENEMY_BALANCE.md` §4.3, `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

**Tests:** `src/audio/effects.test.ts` gains a "Phaser fire-sequence volume" block asserting the 0.5 constant, the per-cue playback volume and the preserved no-gap delays.


## Replan 2026-10-19 — residual audit gap

**Why replanned:** The parent was previously planned (`plan_complete`, 6 children, all terminal) and implemented, but the producer audit on 2026-10-18 was rejected: "The Phaser is still way too loud." The post-audit diagnosis and chosen fix are recorded in the section above, but no child work item covered that fix, so the residual gap was unowned. The parent was returned to `intake_complete` for this replan; the original six children remain completed and are not re-opened.

**New child:** Phaser fire-sequence volume trim + verification (post-audit) (AH-0MVFHE6VP006GEX0) — task, high priority, no dependencies. It carries the test-first ACs (constant + per-cue playback volume + preserved no-gap delays), the `effects.ts` trim, the documentation updates and the verification step. The AC coverage review for the original AC1–AC5 set is unchanged (100% covered, 0 uncovered, 0 conflicts); this child covers the additional post-audit requirement.

**Interview note:** no new clarifying questions were required — the fix (runtime `PHASER_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE = 0.5`, mirroring `TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE`) was already decided and documented in the post-audit section of this description during the audit-response session. The Appendix below records the replan decisions; existing Q1–Q3 answers remain valid and are not re-asked.

### Appendix (replan): questions & answers

- Q: "Is a new child work item required for the Phaser volume trim, or does an existing child cover it?" — Answer (plan, repo + worklog evidence): a new child is required. All six original children are terminal (`completed`/`in_review`) and none of their ACs mention the Phaser runtime volume; the only trace of the fix was the un-owned post-audit section of this description. Evidence: `wl list --parent AH-0MVAUU594007S92Q --json`, `grep PHASER_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE src/audio/effects.ts` (absent).
- Q: "Does the duplicate-work check find an existing item for the Phaser trim?" — Answer: no. `wl search "phaser volume" --json` returns only the Phaser playback rewrite (AH-0MUTYV92Y000WJ8Z, completed), the Tank/Scout volume reduction precedent (AH-0MV74ROYR009X8U3, completed) and this parent; none covers a Phaser fire-sequence trim.
- Q: "Should the fix be baked into assets instead of applied at runtime?" — Answer (producer, post-audit section above): runtime trim, because the baked Phaser assets are already inside the AC2 tier and pinned by the guard; the audible problem is the missing playback trim. Recorded as a deliberate constraint deviation in the child.
- Open question (none blocking): none — the plan can proceed without further producer input.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-17 — initial plan: 6 children created (guard test, analysis report, AC2 tiers, AC3 scale snap, AC4 Scout fire, AC5 validation), 9 dependency edges wired, parent advanced to `plan_complete`.
- 2026-10-19 — replan after producer audit rejection: verified all original children terminal and the original AC1–AC5 coverage still 100%; discovered the post-audit Phaser fix was unowned (no `PHASER_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE` in `src/audio/effects.ts`); created child AH-0MVFHE6VP006GEX0 (test-first ACs, runtime trim, docs, verification); no dependency edges needed (independent of the baked-asset work); parent re-advanced to `plan_complete`. # Audio Design Chapter — retro-arcade survival game GDD

## Problem statement

The GDD currently defines only SFX (§7.3 Audio Direction) and states background music is out of MVP scope with no musical direction defined. The game lacks a documented musical identity (scales, motifs, harmonic language, instrumentation, dynamic mixing, and state-driven music architecture) to guide composition and implementation when music is eventually built.

## Users

- **Audio designers and composers** — need a definitive musical language (scales/modes, motifs, progressions, instrumentation palette) to write consistent, on-brief music.
- **Technical audio programmers** — need the implementation contract (bus architecture, priority tiers, ducking, state machine, middleware guidance) to build or integrate the music system.
- **Game designers / producers** — need per-game-state emotional targets and transition rules to keep audio aligned with gameplay pacing.

User stories:

- As an audio designer, I want documented scales and motifs per game state, so my compositions match the game's emotional arc without guesswork.
- As a technical audio programmer, I want the music state machine and dynamic-mixing rules defined, so I can implement or configure the music engine against a fixed contract.
- As a producer, I want music explicitly scoped as design reference (out of MVP), so the shipped SFX scope (§7.3) is not disturbed.

## Acceptance Criteria

# Dev-mode write-back: gym "Save to repo" persists bot tuning to src/data/bot-tuning.json

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** feature

**discovered-from:** AH-0MV9GZD2C005IIU3 (its scope-creep note flagged this path out of scope there)

## Problem statement

Today the Bot Tuning gym persists only to `localStorage` (`ai-hell-bot-tuning`), and the Git-tracked shipped baseline `src/data/bot-tuning.json` must be refreshed manually via the gym **Export** button → overwrite file → commit (documented in `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §12 and `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`). Player ship and enemy/difficulty configs already have a dev-mode write-back path: the Vite CSV plugin (`vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`, served `/api/csv/...` PUT endpoints) writes gym Save/Save-As edits straight into the committed CSVs (`src/core/configStore.ts` `saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`). This item gives bot tuning the same convenience: a dev-mode (Vite-serve-only) write path that persists the currently-selected tuning configuration to `src/data/bot-tuning.json`, so a designer does not have to Export → overwrite → commit manually.

## Users

- Designer tuning the demo bot in the Bot Tuning gym — wants a Save action that writes current tuning back to the committed baseline (dev server only).
- Maintainer / release reviewer — wants the write path dev-only and explicit, so a production/static build can never mutate the committed baseline.

Example user stories:

- *As a designer tuning the demo bot, I want a Save action in the Bot Tuning gym to write my current tuning back to `src/data/bot-tuning.json` (dev server only), so the shipped baseline stays in sync without the manual Export → overwrite → commit dance.*
- *As a maintainer, I want the write path to be dev-only and explicit, so a production/static build can never mutate the committed baseline or surprise a distributed user.*

## Desired change

1. **Write endpoint** — expose a dev-only endpoint (e.g. `PUT /api/bot-tuning/`) in the Vite dev-server plugin chain, mirroring the `configCsvPlugin` pattern (allowed-path allowlist, atomic write = temp file + rename, `apply: 'serve'` only). The endpoint validates the incoming blob's shape before writing (reuse the store's `parseState`-style validation / `coerceTuningValues`) and writes the exact `serialiseBotTuningState()` JSON blob to `src/data/bot-tuning.json`.
2. **Gym affordance** — add a "Save to repo" (dev-only) button in the Bot Tuning gym panel, next to Export, that posts the current store state to the endpoint and reports success/failure (`SaveResult`-shaped, like `saveShipConfig`). Disabled or hidden outside dev (`import.meta.env.DEV`, matching `saveShipConfig`'s `isDev()` gate).
3. **Out-of-scope guard** — no runtime behaviour change and no new write path in production; same guard contract as the CSV store (`WRITE_UNAVAILABLE` outside dev). Atomic replace must preserve the trailing-newline/pretty-print format the `bot-tuning.json` tests expect (`src/data/bot-tuning.test.ts` asserts byte-identity with the store Export plus trailing newline).
4. **Tests** — unit tests for the write helper (valid blob replaces file; invalid blob rejected without touching the file; non-dev returns unavailable; byte round-trip with `serialiseBotTuningState()`), gym-level test that "Save to repo" calls the write path and reflects a real file write, and a plugin-endpoint test mirroring `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` scope. `npm run typecheck` and the full suite stay green; the gym↔game duplicate-body parity guard stays green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Dev-only write endpoint persists the baseline.** In dev mode, a write of the current `serialiseBotTuningState()` blob updates `src/data/bot-tuning.json` atomically; the file stays byte-identical to the store Export (pretty-print + trailing newline), so `src/data/bot-tuning.test.ts` round-trip tests pass after the write.
- **AC2 — Invalid input never corrupts the file.** A write with an invalid/unschematised blob fails with a clear `SaveResult` reason and leaves the committed file untouched.
- **AC3 — Production/static builds cannot write.** The endpoint is dev-serve-only and the client gate (`isDev()`) means a production build reports `WRITE_UNAVAILABLE` (no mutation of the shipped baseline).
- **AC4 — Gym affordance.** The Bot Tuning gym exposes a dev-only "Save to repo" control that persists the current selection and reports success/failure; hidden/disabled outside dev.
- **AC5 — Tests + validation.** Unit + gym + plugin-endpoint tests cover persistence, rejection, round-trip, and non-dev unavailability; `npm run typecheck`, the full suite, and the parity guard pass.

## Constraints

- No change to bot decision/permission semantics — only a dev-tool persistence path (same scope boundary recorded in AH-0MV9GZD2C005IIU3).
- Follows the CSV plugin precedent exactly (atomic write, allowed-path allowlist, `apply: serve` only); do not invent a new infra pattern.
- The stored file must stay Git-committable and byte-stable (test contract).
- Out of scope: automatic background sync on every slider move (that would spam writes); the affordance must be an explicit Save action.
- Out of scope: any write path in production/static builds; dev-only via Vite serve.

## Existing state

- `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` already exports `serialiseBotTuningState()` (the exact Export blob) and has `parseState`-style (private) schema validation + `coerceTuningValues` from `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`.
- `src/data/bot-tuning.json` is the Git-tracked baseline whose byte-format contract is pinned by `src/data/bot-tuning.test.ts` (pretty-print + trailing newline, byte-identical to fresh-profile Export).
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` is the established dev-write infra: `apply: 'serve'`, `/api/csv/...` GET/PUT, atomic write helper, allowed-path allowlist; registered in `vite.config.ts`.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` defines the `SaveResult` / `WRITE_UNAVAILABLE` / `isDev()` contract the bot-tuning write should mirror.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` already has the Export button/status readout in `_buildActionRow()` and the panel-status helpers; a "Save to repo" button slots in alongside.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — the CSV dev-write pattern to parallel/clone for bot tuning
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` — the plugin-endpoint test harness to mirror
- `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` — `serialiseBotTuningState()`, `parseState`/`coerceTuningValues` validation, `BOT_TUNING_SCHEMA_VERSION`
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig` + `SaveResult`/`WRITE_UNAVAILABLE` contract to mirror
- `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — the committed baseline the dev write targets
- `src/data/bot-tuning.test.ts` — file round-trip/trailing-newline contract the writer must preserve
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` — new "Save to repo" control next to Export
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.test.ts` — gym-level write-path test
- `vite.config.ts` — plugin registration
- Docs: `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §12, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — update the refresh workflow (dev write vs Export)

## Related work

- `Distributed versions of the game do not use the correct Bot definitions (AH-0MV9GZD2C005IIU3)` — completed; introduced the bundled baseline this write-back refreshes; its scope-creep note explicitly deferred this dev-mode write path.
- `Gym scene for AI bot tuning (AH-0MV4D7LAD009XYR0)` — completed; the tuning gym + store.
- `Watch Demo and video recording should fly the saved bot-tuning configuration (AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL)` — completed; Export/`--bot-config` workflow.
- `Config store: in-memory registry, boot load, dev write (AH-0MUE2MGZM0016U3L)` / `Vite CSV plugin: dev middleware (GET/PUT, atomic write, validation) (AH-0MUE2MHRC0090AXP)` — completed; the CSV write-back precedent this item parallels.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "Save to repo" writes the full store state** (`serialiseBotTuningState()` blob, all named configs + current selection), i.e. exactly the Export blob. This is the only format the byte-identity test contract accepts (the shipped file is the whole `{ version, current, configs }` state), so the button's "current selection" phrasing means the current exported state. (If instead only the single selected config should be written, the file-format contract would need revisiting — not expected.)
- **Assumption — endpoint shape** follows the CSV-plugin precedent: a dev-only Vite middleware, PUT `/api/bot-tuning/` (or a parallel path under a bot-tuning prefix), validating before atomic write. Exact path is an implementation decision within the pattern.
- **Risk — stale baseline:** unchanged existing risk; the dev write reduces (does not eliminate) manual-drift by making the refresh an explicit action.
- **Risk — surprise writes:** a designer clicking Save expects a repo mutation; mitigations: dev-only gate, explicit button label + tooltip, `SaveResult` feedback.
- **Scope-creep risk:** automatic background sync on every slider move is out of scope (explicit Save only). Record any follow-up ideas as new work items, not scope.

## Verification of existing information

- Verified in repo: `serialiseBotTuningState()` is exported from `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` (byte-identical Export blob); `coerceTuningValues` exported from `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`; `parseStateObject` is private (a small store change or a plugin-local validator may be needed — implementation detail, not a requirement change).
- Verified in repo: `configCsvPlugin` exports `atomicWrite`, uses `apply: 'serve'`, allowed-path allowlist, and its test suite exercises PUT/atomic/validation via a real ephemeral HTTP server with `serve`/`build` modes — the exact harness to mirror.
- Verified in repo: `GymBotTuning._buildActionRow()` already builds Export + status; `GymPlayer._onSave()` shows the `saveShipConfig` status-reporting pattern to mirror.
- Duplicate check performed — no overlapping item found (searches: "write-back", "save to repo", "config write"; the closest completed items are the CSV write-back precedent and the scoped-out parent note).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: None required — the seed context (detailed discovered-from description) sufficed to draft a clear brief; the repo confirms the referenced APIs and file-format contract. Assumptions above are flagged for producer confirmation rather than asked, per the intake rule to not ask answerable-by-repo questions.
- Open question (advisory, not blocking): endpoint shape — preferred option **parallel dev-only middleware mirroring `configCsvPlugin`** (explicit path, keeps CSV plugin untouched and its tests stable); alternative is extending the CSV plugin's allowlist (rejected: not a CSV, and would complicate the CSV plugin's schema).

## Goal

A stock `npm run dev` (no special env vars) collects the run's telemetry to the local JSONL

# Game-side uploader fired at run end

Child of **Dev-mode telemetry upload to dev server with automatic evaluation** (AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN).

## Goal

At run end, when dev mode is active and the share-telemetry setting is on, the game POSTs the
local JSONL sink's accumulated telemetry to the same-origin dev server — fire-and-forget, never
blocking or crashing the game.

## User story

As a maintainer, I want every dev-mode run to deliver its recording to the dev server
automatically at run end, with zero manual export.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new game-side module (e.g. `src/telemetry/devUpload.ts`) exports an upload function that:
  - returns a no-op when the dev gate (F1) is false (non-dev or setting off);
  - reads the accumulated `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl` localStorage content;
  - POSTs it same-origin to `POST /api/telemetry/upload` (endpoint name from F5), body
    `text/plain`/`application/x-ndjson` with the settings/env composition asserted in tests;
  - catches **all** errors (network failure, HTTP non-2xx, empty storage) and never throws.
- Storage/fetch are injected seams so tests need no network or real localStorage.
- `PlayScene._finishRun()` flushes the recorder (`await runTelemetry.flush()` — new async bridge
  via `void this.flushAndUploadDevTelemetry()`), then invokes the uploader fire-and-forget;
  the GameOverScene transition still happens regardless of the upload outcome.
- Tests: fires with the sink content when dev+on; no fetch when dev+off or prod; empty storage ⇒
  no request; rejected fetch ⇒ resolves without throwing; non-2xx ⇒ swallowed; the run-end hook
  still transitions to GameOverScene; the sink's localStorage content is left intact after upload
  (parent constraint — assert no clear-after-upload).

# Intake Brief — Increase the number of waves in the levels, add mini-bosses

**Work item:** AH-0MVCC8XSS007P01Z (epic, high)
**Headline:** Grow the campaign to exactly 10 waves per level (100 waves over 10
levels), add a bespoke mini-boss as the 10th wave of every level, introduce 10
net-new alien archetypes, 5 net-new power-ups and 5 net-new weapon types spread
across the levels, and wrap it in a mini-boss reward loop (upgrade an owned
permanent weapon/power-up **or** unlock a new weapon type from a ~50%-locked
pool) plus a checkpoint save/resume at each mini-boss.

## Problem statement

The shipped campaign has only 2–4 waves per level (29 waves total across 10
levels) and a single final boss after Level 10 — there is no mid-level payoff,
no escalation hook within a level, and no way to resume a run. The operator
wants every level to feel substantial (10 waves), each level to end in a
bespoke mini-boss that grants a meaningful permanent reward, the campaign to
offer genuinely new content for the later levels, and the player to be able to
pick the run up again after closing the game instead of starting over.

## Users

- **Player** — "As a player, I want each of the 10 levels to take 10 waves and
  end in a mini-boss, so the campaign keeps escalating within every level."
- **Player** — "As a player, I want a mini-boss kill to let me choose between
  upgrading one of my permanent weapons/power-ups and unlocking a new weapon
  type, so my ship keeps growing in the direction I choose."
- **Player** — "As a player, I want the game to save my progress at every
  mini-boss so I can close the game and resume from the last checkpoint
  instead of starting a new game."
- **Designer/content author** — "As a designer, I want 10 new alien archetypes,
  5 new power-ups and 5 new weapons spread across the 10 levels — alongside
  the existing roster — so the later levels introduce genuinely new content
  while every previous level's enemies can still appear."
- **Engineer** — "As an engineer, I want the new behaviour (mini-bosses,
  rewards, unlocks) to run through the shared core and be mirrored in the gym
  scenes, so gym↔game parity holds without divergent copies."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **10 waves per level, mini-boss as the 10th wave** — Every level 1–10 has
   exactly 10 waves; the 10th wave of each level is that level's mini-boss
   encounter (9 regular waves + mini-boss). The final boss still triggers
   after Level 10. Wave counts and progression are data-driven
   (`src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` / `LEVELS`) and verified by tests.
2. **Net-new content for later levels** — At least 10 net-new alien
   archetypes, 5 net-new power-ups and 5 net-new weapon types are added beyond
   today's catalogue (17 enemies / 11 power-ups / 11 weapons → ≥27 / ≥16 / ≥16),
   spread across the levels as appropriate, each exercised in a gym scene
   (gym↔game parity).
3. **Mini-boss reward** — Defeating each mini-boss grants exactly ONE choice:
   upgrade any 1 owned permanent weapon/power-up by one level, **or** unlock a
   new weapon type from the locked pool. ~50% of the weapon/power-up catalogue
   is locked at Level 1 and becomes available through these mini-boss rewards.
   The choice is applied through the existing permanent-level machinery and
   choice overlay (`MineralChoiceScene`, `powerups/choice`).
4. **Checkpoint save/resume** — A checkpoint (level, wave, lives, score,
   minerals, permanent upgrade levels, unlocked weapons) is auto-saved to
   `localStorage` at each mini-boss; the main menu offers Continue/resume from
   the last checkpoint in addition to New Game; starting a new game clears it.
5. **Quality & documentation** — The full project test suite passes with the
   changes; campaign invariants (difficulty non-decreasing, level variety,
   archetype reuse) continue to hold with 10-wave levels; all related
   documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
   `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`,
   and the README.

## Constraints

- **Mini-boss is the 10th wave** (not an 11th phase) — 9 regular waves plus the
  mini-boss as wave 10 of each level (producer Q2).
- **Content is net-new** — the 10 aliens / 5 power-ups / 5 weapons are beyond
  the current catalogue, not counted against it (producer Q1).
- **One reward choice per mini-boss** (upgrade an owned item OR unlock a new
  weapon type); ~50% of weapon/power-up catalogue locked at Level 1
  (producer Q3).
- **Gym↔game parity** — gameplay changes must be mirrored in the gym scenes
  via the shared core; no divergent copies (AGENTS.md).
- Persistence follows the existing `localStorage` convention
  (`ai_hell_*` keys alongside settings/leaderboard).
- No CHANGELOG.md edits (managed by the ship release pipeline).

## Risks, assumptions & failure modes

- **Scope creep (content volume)** — 10 wave rows × 10 levels plus 10 aliens + 5 power-ups + 5 weapons + 10 mini-boss designs is large. Mitigation: treat this as an epic decomposed under the plan skill; content is data-driven and additive, so per-item ACs can land incrementally. Record extra opportunities (e.g. more archetypes, boss-specific audio) as linked work items, not scope.
- **Difficulty-curve rebalancing** — widening levels to 10 waves each changes the non-decreasing difficulty curve and wave-gating invariants. Mitigation: extend `difficulty-curves.csv` monotonically and keep/re-run the campaign invariant tests (`campaignInvariants.test.ts`, `campaignBalanceAudit.test.ts`, `campaignRoster.test.ts`).
- **Balance** — 10-wave levels and mini-bosses lengthen runs; assumed acceptable (producer Q2), but difficulty tuning is expected during implementation. Assumption: wave-10 target difficulty sits above the level's regular waves but below the following level's opening.
- **Unlock pool definition** — "~50% of the weapon/power-up catalogue" needs a concrete locked set. Assumption: the locked set is defined in data at implementation time, biased toward newly added and later-level items, and includes enough early options that a Level-1 player still sees choice.
- **Checkpoint scope** — saves permanent levels/unlocks and run state. Risk: checkpoint/continue interacting with telemetry, run-seed reproduction and leaderboard scoring. Mitigation: checkpoint stores the run seed and permanent progression; leaderboard entries from resumed runs remain valid via the existing serialisation path.
- **Save-compatibility** — a checkpoint written by an earlier build must not crash a later build. Mitigation: defensive parsing with safe defaults (same pattern as the `Leaderboard` corrupt-JSON fallback).
- Assumption: "all previous level enemy types can appear in higher levels" already holds via the sequencer and remains a constraint on the expanded levels (existing archetype-reuse invariant is kept).

## Existing state

- Levels: 10 already exist (`MAX_LEVEL = 10`, `BOSS_LEVEL = 11`); campaign is
  currently **29 waves** total (L1=2, L2=3, L3=3, L4=3, L5=2, L6=4, L7=4,
  L8=3, L9=3, L10=2), driven by `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` +
  hand-authored `LEVELS` in `src/waves/Formations.ts`.
- Enemies: 17 archetypes ship today (scout, diver, tank, phaser, swarm,
  asteroid, harvester + classic-arcade march, capturer, ghost-chase/ambush/
  flank/wander, grunt, raider, lane-traffic, orbital-strike). Levels 6–10
  already showcase the classic-arcade roster (AH-0MV29SBAQ000HQR2).
- Power-ups: 11 (shield, bomb, speed_boost, phase_shift, teleport, extra_life,
  magnet, mineral_scoop, smart_bomb, force_field, mystery_ufo). Weapons: 11
  (cannon, spread, dual, rapid, wave_laser, ricochet, cluster, options, nova,
  mortar, arc).
- A permanent/temporary level split exists (`powerUpLevels.ts`,
  AH-0MUX802450085VZZ / AH-0MUX9T7C7003CBQP): hold-full rewards raise the
  permanent level for the run. A reusable choice overlay exists
  (`MineralChoiceScene` + `powerups/choice`).
- No mini-boss concept, no weapon/power-up unlock gating, and no run
  checkpoint/save (only settings, leaderboard and rules persist).

## Desired change

- Extend the campaign data to 10 waves per level (per-level mini-boss as wave
  10), keeping hand-authored `fixed`/`dynamic` mixing where it adds value.
- Add a per-level mini-boss wave/phase: WaveManager recognises the 10th wave
  of each level as a mini-boss encounter; PlayScene spawns the mini-boss,
  handles its defeat, and only then advances to the next level.
- Add 10 net-new alien archetypes, 5 net-new power-ups and 5 net-new weapon
  types, spread across the 10 levels (data + entities + spawners + gyms).
- Add the mini-boss reward: on mini-boss defeat, launch the choice overlay for
  exactly one choice (upgrade owned permanent item OR unlock a weapon type from
  the ~50%-locked pool); apply through existing permanent-level machinery.
- Add checkpoint save/resume: save at each mini-boss to `localStorage`;
  expose Continue from the main menu; clear on New Game.

## Key Files

- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — extend to 10 rows per level; mark the
  10th wave as the mini-boss wave.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — `LEVELS` skeleton + per-level mini-boss wave
  entries.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — recognise mini-boss wave; boss-gating per level;
  progression to next level only on mini-boss defeat.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — spawn mini-boss at wave 10; launch reward choice;
  write checkpoints; resume path.
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` — Continue/resume entry point.
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`, `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` + new
  entity/spawner modules (`src/waves/`, `src/entities/`) — 10 net-new alien
  archetypes + 10 mini-boss designs.
- `src/powerups/types.ts`, `src/utils/weapons.ts` — 5 net-new power-ups /
  5 net-new weapon types (IDs, catalogue entries, level curves).
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — permanent-level application for the
  upgrade path; unlock state for the locked pool.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts`, `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — reuse the
  choice overlay for the mini-boss reward (already launcher-agnostic).
- New checkpoint store module (e.g. `src/core/checkpointStore.ts`) + keys
  alongside `ai_hell_settings` / `ai_hell_leaderboard`.
- `src/scenes/gym/` — parity gyms for new aliens, weapons, power-ups and a
  mini-boss gym (pattern: `GymBoss.ts`).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`,
  `README.md` — update wave tables, enemy/power-up/weapon catalogues, save-data
  section.

## Related work

- AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5 / AH-0MT7QQGBU008V4R0 — Game Design Document (10-level
  campaign, boss, power-up catalogues; save-data design §6.6).
- AH-0MU72ZK3P006CH9G — WaveManager wave/level progression (extension point).
- AH-0MV29SBAQ000HQR2 — 5 new levels showcasing the classic-arcade roster
  (existing later-level content; the "net-new" bar is measured beyond it).
- AH-0MUX802450085VZZ / AH-0MUX9T7C7003CBQP — permanent/temporary power-up and
  weapon level split (reward machinery basis).
- AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q — hold-full choice scene (`MineralChoiceScene`),
  reusable for the mini-boss reward.
- AH-0MUZMTSQF0054WI8 — dedicated boss-hit SFX cue (pattern for mini-boss
  audio).
- find-related report appended to this work item's description.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "At least 10 new aliens, 5 new power-ups, 5 new weapon types for the
  later levels" — measured against the current catalogue or net-new beyond it?
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): "net new — spread them across levels as you
  feel appropriate". Source: interactive reply on the work item. Research:
  current catalogue is 17 enemies / 11 power-ups / 11 weapons (verified in
  `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`, `src/powerups/types.ts`,
  `src/utils/weapons.ts`); the classic-arcade roster (AH-0MV29SBAQ000HQR2) is
  existing content, not counted toward the net-new bar.
- Q2: Is the mini-boss the 10th wave or an encounter after 10 regular waves?
  One shared mini-boss scaled per level, or bespoke per-level designs?
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): "10th wave, 10 designs". Source: interactive
  reply. Interpretation: mini-boss **is** wave 10 of each level (9 regular
  waves + mini-boss), and there are 10 bespoke mini-boss designs, one per
  level.
- Q3: Reward + save model (reconcile the two reward sentences and the
  checkpoint requirement) — Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): "as recommended".
  Source: interactive reply. Recommended model (accepted): each mini-boss
  defeat grants ONE choice — upgrade any 1 owned permanent weapon/power-up by
  one level, OR unlock a new weapon type from the locked pool; ~50% of the
  weapon/power-up catalogue locked at Level 1, unlocked via mini-boss rewards;
  checkpoint auto-saved at each mini-boss (level, lives, score, minerals,
  permanent upgrade levels, unlocked weapons) to `localStorage`, with Continue/
  resume on the main menu.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On the frame `isPhased` rises, the treatment emits a brief ripple/burst (short sharp chromatic-split surge with a flicker step, ≈150–250 ms) that reads as a glitch hit and is visually distinct from player-death juice — no camera shake; the existing screen-wide dim + split overlays are retained.
